(1) MPMP with a particular schedule is an effective inference engine for HNC, and (2) MPMP can be used to implement fast inference for HCN and to add supervision information, and (3) HCN’s learned features are different than the ones learned by CNNs.

(1) HCN can discover hierarchical compositional features in a set of images without supervision; and (2) HCN’s fast inference can be used for image classification with exactly the same functional architecture of a convolutional network.

(i) MPMP with a particular schedule is a fast, exact inference engine for HCP; (ii) fast HCN inference has exactly the same form as a CNN with linear activations and a particular weight initialization; (iii) HCN’s features have a hierarchical compositional structure that is qualitatively different from the features learned by a CNN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to learn a hierarchical compositional model of binary data and how to use the model for inference, learning, classification, and inpainting.
the question of whether we can build a generative model that can learn the building blocks of an image in a hierarchical manner, without supervision.

the following: (1) the discovery of compositional features in binary images, (2) a new inference algorithm for a new model, and (3) a new model that has a functional form similar to a CNN but with qualitatively different features.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCN is a new and promising approach to unsupervised learning of features that can be applied to a variety of problems in computer vision.
HCN is a new model that is very similar to a CNN with linear activations, except that the features it learns are much more interpretable and hierarchical.
HCN is to CNN as a belief net is to a logistic regressor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to do feature learning in a CNN without the use of any non-linearity, and without the use of back-propagation.

we have a new model that can learn features that are qualitatively different from those learned by a convolutional neural net, and we have a new inference method that is able to learn the model parameters and infer the latent variables in a single step.
HCNs can learn the same features as a CNN, but in a much more principled manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HCN can learn features in the style of CNNs but with a different objective: to explain the data using a small number of binary features that are hierarchically composed and disentangled.
the features learned by HCN are much easier for humans to understand than the features learned by CNNs, and this makes it easier to understand the classification decisions.
HCN is a very flexible model that can be used to learn and represent a wide range of features.
